title: MODE 5 ▶ 2: Quad (Quadratic Regression)
summary: Enter x , y DT for at least 3 pairs, press AC, then recall A, B, C. Fitted parabola: y = A + Bx + Cx².

body.text: Quad fits a parabola y = A + Bx + Cx² to paired data. Use when the trend bends once (a single peak or valley) — trajectories, symmetric curves, or any scatter that is not well served by a straight line.
Quadratic regression fits y = A + Bx + Cx² — a parabola. Use it when the trend bends once (a single peak or valley). The calculator recalls A, B, and C (item 3 is C, not r).

body.caption: Sample fit y = x² − 2x + 3 through five points. The curve has a minimum near x = 1.

body.text: Open Quad regression (MODE 5, ▶, then 2). Clear old data, then enter each pair as x , y DT using the M+ (DT) key. You need at least three points. When they are all registered, press AC once to leave the list.

body.title: Enter data
items: SHIFT 9 → 1 EXE if replacing an old list
For each point: x , y DT (comma between x and y, then DT)
After the third (or more) pair: AC once
Do not recall A, B, C until after AC

body.lead: Example — three points on y = x² − 2x + 3:

body.text: Minimum 3 pairs (three unknowns A, B, C). With exactly three non-collinear points the fit is exact. More points give a least-squares parabola.
After AC, the calculator has fitted y = A + Bx + Cx². Recall A, B, and C with SHIFT 2 → 1 (VAR) → ▶ → ▶, then 1 / 2 / 3 EXE. Quad has no r; item 3 on that screen is C.

items: ŷ for a given x: type x, SHIFT 2 → 1 → ◀ → 3 EXE
x̂ from y (two roots): type y, SHIFT 2 → 1 → ◀ → 1 EXE and ◀ → 2 EXE

body.text: Write the answer as y = A + Bx + Cx² using your recalled values. For the example above: A = 3, B = −2, C = 1 → y = 3 − 2x + x².
